value.rationale: The newly complete dyadic count and quartic stopping-time sum answer the natural question of how numerous and how slow the terminating exceptional basin is. The conditional square-root law quantifies typical zero-hitting time at quadratic-logarithmic scale. Its provably sharp O((log X)^-1/2) Kolmogorov rate reveals a genuine boundary-layer effect from early halvings; this is not just an unmotivated finite table or a renaming of deterministic membership results.
